messages.content:
Classify these policies:

1. Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment: AI systems must not be used for making clinical decisions, determining diagnoses, or treatment plans. Clinicians remain personally accountable for all decisions regarding patient care, and AI outputs require validation before use.
2. Protected Health Information: No person-identifiable data may be input to public AI tools. No business-sensitive or confidential data processing is allowed. Combined details of a local area, a rare disease, and a very young age may enable a patient to be identified, requiring careful anonymisation assessment.
3. Medical Professional Impersonation: AI systems must not be used for generating clinical entries directly into patient records or replacing professional judgment. The final responsibility for diagnosis, treatment, and patient care rests with the clinician, and over-reliance on AI without oversight may compromise patient safety.
